Session 0: Getting Started

Setup, File Downloads & How to Use This Workshop

Author

Immanuel Williams

Published

August 5, 2026

Welcome

Welcome to the API Workshop! Before we dive into the content, this document will help you get oriented — who is here to help, where to find things, how to download your working files, and what to do if you get stuck.

The workshop front page includes a short introduction to Meg, our student assistant, and me, your instructor. You only need that once at the start, so the team introduction link lives on the front page rather than inside every session.

Workshop Overview

This workshop runs across two days and four sessions. Each session builds on the last, so we recommend following them in order.

By the end of the course, you should be able to:

  1. Understand the flow of an API, then zoom in more specifically on a response.
  2. Understand how to make a request.
  3. Make your first API call.
  4. Decide what you can do with the data returned by an API.
Day Time Session Focus
Day 1 (8/5) 8:00–9:00 AM Session 1 JSON Fundamentals & Request/Response
Day 1 (8/5) 9:00–10:00 AM Session 2 CRUD, HTTP Methods & URL Anatomy
Day 2 (8/6) 9:00–10:00 AM Session 3 Weather API — Setup, Current Weather, Geocoding
Day 2 (8/6) 10:00–11:00 AM Session 4 Historical Weather, Visualization & Wrap-Up

What We Assume You Already Know

This workshop assumes you have seen the following before Day 1. You do not need to be an expert — “I’ve done it a few times” is enough:

  • Running R code — executing a line or chunk and reading the output
  • Assigning variables — x <- 5
  • Calling functions with arguments — round(3.14, digits = 1)
  • Data frames — rows, columns, and looking at one with head() or View()
  • The pipe |> — passing a result into the next function (we’ll remind you as we go)
  • A basic ggplot() — we will supply all plotting code, but it helps if it isn’t your first time seeing it

You do not need to know: anything about APIs, JSON, HTTP, URLs beyond typing one into a browser, httr2, or purrr::map(). Those are what the workshop teaches.

If several items in the first list feel shaky, skim a refresher before Day 1 — for example the first chapters of R for Data Science.

Quick Survey — Help Us Tailor the Workshop

Please answer these before Day 1 (we will also ask by show of hands at the start):

  1. Your R experience:
    1. New to R (less than a semester of use)
    2. Comfortable — I use R for my own courses or analysis
    3. Advanced — I teach with R and write my own functions
  2. How do you plan to use this workshop? (e.g., adding live data to an intro stats course, a data science elective, student projects, your own research)
  3. How will you follow along during the sessions?
    1. Online — reading the session pages on this website
    2. Positron/RStudio — working in the source (text) editor
    3. Positron/RStudio — working in the visual editor

There is no wrong answer to 3 — but knowing the split helps us pace the live coding.

Step 1 — Download Your Workshop Folder

Download the complete student folder:

Download all student QMD files

Move the downloaded zip file to a convenient location, such as your Desktop, and unzip it. Work directly from the extracted api_workshop_empty/ folder so the session files and their image assets keep the directory structure they need.

The extracted folder contains:

api_workshop_empty/
├── 01_JSON_and_Request_Response.qmd
├── 02_CRUD_HTTP_Methods_URL.qmd
├── 03_Weather_API_Setup.qmd
├── 04_Historical_Weather_Visualization.qmd
├── README.md
└── images/

Why this matters: R and Quarto look for files relative to the .qmd files. Keeping the downloaded structure intact means the workshop files work without changing paths.

If the zip download is blocked on your computer, put your hand up and we will help you get the same student folder.

How to get started:

  1. Click the download link above.
  2. Move the zip file to your Desktop or another convenient location.
  3. Unzip it and leave everything inside the extracted folder.

Step 2 — Open the File in Positron

  1. Open Positron (or RStudio)
  2. Go to File → Open File…
  3. Navigate to the extracted api_workshop_empty/ folder and open the session file for today

You do not need to open a project — just open the .qmd file directly.

If You Get Stuck

If you have a question during the workshop, put your hand up and Meg will help. If you get stuck on one of the questions, the online version is also here for you.

All session content — including completed code — is available on this website.

Use the Sessions menu in the navigation bar at the top of this page to browse any session. Each page shows the full document with all code blocks visible, so you can reference it at any point during the workshop.

You are encouraged to try the exercises yourself first, then check the website if you need a hint or want to verify your answer.

Tools Checklist

Before Day 1, confirm you have the following installed:

install.packages(c("httr2", "tibble", "dplyr", "purrr", "ggplot2", "glue"))

Questions?

Reach out before or during the workshop. We will also leave time at the start of each session to resolve any setup issues.

See you there!

## What We Assume You Already Know

This workshop assumes you have seen the following **before** Day 1. You do not need to be an expert — "I've done it a few times" is enough:

- **Running R code** — executing a line or chunk and reading the output
- **Assigning variables** — `x <- 5`
- **Calling functions with arguments** — `round(3.14, digits = 1)`
- **Data frames** — rows, columns, and looking at one with `head()` or `View()`
- **The pipe** `|>` — passing a result into the next function (we'll remind you as we go)
- **A basic `ggplot()`** — we will supply all plotting code, but it helps if it isn't your first time seeing it

**You do *not* need to know:** anything about APIs, JSON, HTTP, URLs beyond typing one into a browser, `httr2`, or `purrr::map()`. Those are what the workshop teaches.

If several items in the first list feel shaky, skim a refresher before Day 1 — for example the first chapters of [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/).

## Tools Checklist

Before Day 1, confirm you have the following installed:

- [ ] **R** (version 4.2 or later) — [download here](https://cran.r-project.org)
- [ ] **Positron** or **RStudio** — [Positron download](https://positron.posit.co)
- [ ] **Required R packages** — run the block below once to install everything

```{r install-packages}
install.packages(c("httr2", "tibble", "dplyr", "purrr", "ggplot2", "glue"))
```

- [x] **API key — not needed!** We use the free [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/) weather API, which requires no sign-up, no key, and no credit card. (The optional Practice Labs use APIs that do require keys — those labs walk you through it.)
